lab_title: Visualizing VSEPR Theory: From Electron Domains to Molecular Geometry
top_level_objectives: Understand that electron domains minimize repulsion to determine electron domain geometry.
Distinguish between electron domain geometry and molecular geometry when lone pairs are present.
Explain why lone pairs cause bond angle deviations from idealized geometries.
Correctly predict shapes for molecules based on their Lewis structure.

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the concept of electron domain repulsion.
key_visuals: A central atom with floating glowing spheres representing electron domains (balloons).
student_actions: Drag and drop spheres onto a central atom to see them automatically space themselves out to maximize distance.
Observe how they snap into the linear (2) and trigonal planar (3) geometries.

scenes.brief_purpose: Explore the tetrahedral, trigonal bipyramidal, and octahedral electron domain geometries.
key_visuals: Interactive 3D models of geometries with dynamic bond-angle markers.
student_actions: Add additional domains to reach 4, 5, and 6 total domains.
Rotate the geometries in 3D space to examine the spatial arrangements and symmetry.

scenes.brief_purpose: Demonstrate how lone pairs occupy more space than bonding pairs.
key_visuals: Comparison of a bonding pair (tight, focused) vs. a lone pair (diffuse, larger orbital cloud).
student_actions: Swap a bonding pair for a lone pair and observe the 'orbital cloud' size difference.
Adjust the bond angles slightly to see how the lone pair 'pushes' on the remaining bonds.

scenes.brief_purpose: Predict molecular geometry by hiding lone pairs.
key_visuals: The tetrahedral geometry of methane compared to the ammonia and water structures.
student_actions: Select 'Hide Lone Pairs' to visualize only the atoms and bonds (e.g., seeing how tetrahedral becomes bent in water).
Name the resulting shape based on the remaining atomic positions.

scenes.brief_purpose: Connect theoretical models to real-world molecular examples.
key_visuals: Overlaying theoretical VSEPR models on high-resolution 3D models of real molecules.
student_actions: Select a real molecule (e.g., PF5, XeF4) and attempt to match it with the correct underlying electron geometry.
Compare the idealized 109.5° bond angle to the experimental measurement of water's 104.5°.

key_visuals: A series of mystery Lewis structures floating in the AR space.
student_actions: Identify the electron domain geometry and molecular geometry for three randomly generated molecules.
Validate answers by seeing the model transform into its predicted shape.
